result.title: GainCtrl: Predicting Remaining Gains for Efficient LLM Agent Execution
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to power agents that interact with tools and environments to solve complex tasks. Repeated attempts improve the quality of tool-using agents, but continued execution incurs additional costs even when it is unlikely to improve the best result ultimately returned. This raises the question of when to stop an attempt to reduce execution cost while preserving task-level Best-of-N quality. To address this question, we introduce GainCtrl, a gain-based execution controller for LLMs. In GainCtrl, a lightweight CPU predictor uses interaction histories to estimate expected positive gains over retained scores, which are then used to guide stopping decisions with calibrated thresholds to limit the loss in mean Best-of-N task quality. We evaluate the controller through trajectory replay across three environments and three LLM actors. Comparisons of interpolated quality-cost Pareto frontiers show that GainCtrl generally uses fewer tokens than baselines at matched target quality. Fixed policies also achieve quality close to that of full execution while substantially reducing token consumption. The predictor runs at millisecond latency on a single CPU thread, supporting repeated monitoring without access to LLM internals.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GainCtrl：用一个轻量 CPU 预测器从交互历史估计相对保留分数的期望正向增益，并以校准阈值决定何时停止重复尝试，从而在保持 Best-of-N 任务质量的同时减少 token 消耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「继续执行的期望增益 vs 成本」量化思路与校准停止准则，可能可供核查迁移到 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK 何时停止的决策；但该工作为纯文本工具型 agent，未涉及视觉证据筛选或 latent 状态分析。
